Decontaminate using decontPro

Source: R/decontPro.R
decontPro.Rd

Decontaminate using decontPro

Usage

decontPro(filtered_counts, cellType, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SingleCellExperiment'
decontPro(
  filtered_counts,
  cellType,
  deltaSd = 2e-05,
  backgroundSd = 2e-06,
  background = NULL,
  ...,
  iter = 50000,
  seed = 12345,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# S4 method for class 'Seurat'
decontPro(
  filtered_counts,
  cellType,
  deltaSd = 2e-05,
  backgroundSd = 2e-06,
  background = NULL,
  ...,
  iter = 50000,
  seed = 12345,
  verbose = TRUE
)

# S4 method for class 'ANY'
decontPro(
  filtered_counts,
  cellType,
  deltaSd = 2e-05,
  backgroundSd = 2e-06,
  background = NULL,
  ...,
  iter = 50000,
  seed = 12345,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

filtered_counts

Count matrix NxM (feature x droplet) with only filtered droplets after cell calling, with at least 2 ADTs and 2 droplets. The counts must be non-negative whole numbers with no NA. If this is a SingleCellExperiment or a Seurat object, expect counts in the assay slot. Split counts layers of a Seurat v5 assay are joined first, so the droplets follow Cells().

cellType

Vector of length M giving the cell type of each droplet, with no NA. Any labels can be used, such as integers, character strings or a factor. The rows of r_est in the returned parameters follow the sorted labels, or a factor's levels with unused levels dropped. Alias: cell_type.

...

Only the aliases cell_type, delta_sd, background_sd and ambient_counts, which can be used in place of cellType, deltaSd, backgroundSd and background. Giving both names of an argument, or any other argument, stops with an error.

deltaSd

Standard deviation of the half-normal prior on how much the ambient contamination levels vary around each droplet's mean level. Smaller values keep the levels of a droplet closer together. Default 2e-5. Alias: delta_sd.

backgroundSd

Standard deviation of the half-normal prior on how much the levels of the model's background component vary around each ADT's mean level. This background is part of the model, not the background counts. Default 2e-6. Alias: background_sd.

background

Count matrix (feature x droplet) of empty droplets, used to estimate the ambient ADT profile; without it, the profile comes from filtered_counts. Only each ADT's total across these droplets (the row sums) is used, pooled into one ambient profile, so the droplets must be empty. Droplets whose barcodes (column names) are also in filtered_counts are removed, so the raw matrix with every barcode can be given. When either has no column names, nothing is removed, with a warning. A warning is also given when no barcode matches but background has at least a tenth as many droplets as there are cells with at least the median cell's total count, as a raw matrix does when the two name the same barcodes differently. Barcodes are matched across all droplets, so with several samples they must be unique across samples, for example with a sample prefix in both. Similar to filtered_counts, if it is a wrapper object, expect counts in the assay slot. When both have row names, its rows are matched to the ADTs of filtered_counts by name: ADTs that aren't in filtered_counts are dropped, and every ADT of filtered_counts must be present. Otherwise the rows are matched by position. The ADTs used must have no NA or negative counts, and some counts in total. Default NULL. Alias: ambient_counts.

iter

Maximum number of iterations of Stan's variational inference. The fit usually stops earlier, when it converges; each iteration takes longer on larger data. Default 50000.

seed

Seed for Stan's random number generator, a whole number from 0 to .Machine$integer.max. Default 12345.

verbose

Whether to print messages and Stan's progress. With FALSE, Stan's output is shown only if the fit fails. Default TRUE.

Value

A list. Each count of filtered_counts is split into three parts, which add up to it:

decontaminated_counts

The native part: the counts from the cell's own proteins. An ADT x droplet matrix with the row and column names of filtered_counts.

ambient_counts

The ambient part, a matrix like decontaminated_counts.

background_counts

The part from the model's background component, a matrix like decontaminated_counts.

parameters

A list of the model's estimates: delta_sd and background_sd, the values of deltaSd and backgroundSd used; r_est, the native ADT profile of each cell type (cell type x ADT, rows named by the cellType labels, each row summing to 1); p_est, the ambient ADT profile (one value per ADT, summing to 1, named by the row names of the matrix it comes from, if any); delta_est, the weight of the ambient profile in the non-background part of each ADT in each droplet, the native profile getting the rest (ADT x droplet); delta_mean_est, its mean level in each droplet; background_est, the background as a proportion of the droplet's total count (ADT x droplet); and background_mean_est, its mean level for each ADT. The ADTs and droplets of these estimates are named by the row and column names of filtered_counts, if it has them.

Examples

# Simulated counts of 10 ADTs (rows) in 8 droplets (columns)
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(80, lambda = 20), nrow = 10)

# Name the droplets by their barcodes
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", 1:8)

# The cell type of each droplet
cellTypes <- c("A", "A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B", "B")

# Simulated counts of the same 10 ADTs in 8 empty droplets (optional)
emptyDroplets <- matrix(rpois(80, lambda = 2), nrow = 10)
colnames(emptyDroplets) <- paste0("empty", 1:8)

# Decontaminate the counts
out <- decontPro(counts, cellTypes, background = emptyDroplets)
